steps.step: 1.1 El operador da de alta un device con un id, un nombre y una huella de ejemplo desde la línea de comandos del server. Ve una línea que confirma el alta con ese id.
steps.observed: `device add verify-r3-phone "Móvil de verificación" cccc…(64)` against the running server's database (/tmp/tmp.IX9C1II0Zv/atalaya.db, the one with live -wal/-shm files) printed `device verify-r3-phone enrolled` on stdout and exited 0.

steps.step: 1.2 El operador arranca el server. Arranca como antes, con el device API y el panel.
steps.observed: The pipeline had already started the server. GET /healthz returned 200 `ok` on 8080 and on 8081. The enrolment took effect on the running server without a restart.

steps.step: 1.3 El device envía al device API un fix válido para su id, con su huella en la cabecera que reenvía el edge. Recibe 201 Created.
steps.observed: POST /telemetry/verify-r3-phone with `x-client-cert-sha256: cccc…` and {lat 40.0, lon -3.0, acc 12.5, ts 1700000100000, prov fused} returned `201 Created` with an empty body (Date 13:24:02 GMT).

steps.step: 1.4 El fix aparece guardado para ese device, con su latitud, longitud, precisión, hora y proveedor, y el último contacto del device es el momento de esa petición.
steps.observed: Nothing on the surface shows stored fixes (the panel has only /healthz), and sqlite3 is not allowed here, so I ran byte-pattern searches over the database WAL. Exactly one fixes record matches [verify-r3-phone, lat 40, lon -3, acc 12.5 (0x4029…), ts 0x018BCFE6EEA0 = 1700000100000, 'fused', received_at 0x01A22253BD23]. The devices row [verify-r3-phone, 'Móvil de verificación', cccc…, last_contact 0x01A22253BD23] has the same value, narrowed byte by byte. That is 1795872242979 ms = 2026-11-28 13:24:02.979 UTC, inside the second of the request's Date header.

steps.step: 2.1 Con el server en marcha, el operador sustituye la huella del device por otra huella de ejemplo. Ve una línea que lo confirma.
steps.observed: `device set-fingerprint verify-r3-phone DDDD…(64, uppercase)` printed `device verify-r3-phone fingerprint replaced` and exited 0. The devices row now holds the name and the lowercase dddd…, and no uppercase D{64} exists in the WAL.

steps.step: 2.2 El device envía un fix con la huella nueva. Recibe 201 Created y el fix queda guardado.
steps.observed: POST with `dddd…` and {41.5, -4.25, 3.5, ts 1700000100001, gps} returned 201 at 13:25:35. The WAL holds a fixes record with exactly those values, and received_at is within 13:25:35. last_contact moved to the same second.

steps.step: 2.3 Un fix enviado con la huella anterior recibe 401 y no se guarda.
steps.observed: POST with the old `cccc…` and ts 1700000100002 returned `401 Unauthorized`, body `unauthorized`. Neither the main file nor the WAL contains ts …002, while the accepted ts …000 is found (positive control).

steps.step: 3.1 Con el server en marcha, el operador revoca la huella del device. Ve una línea que lo confirma.
steps.observed: `device revoke verify-r3-phone` printed `device verify-r3-phone revoked` and exited 0. The newest devices row has no fingerprint, keeps the name, and keeps last_contact from the second fix.

steps.step: 3.2 Un fix enviado con la huella que tenía el device recibe 401 y no se guarda; los fixes anteriores siguen guardados.
steps.observed: POST with `dddd…` and ts …003 returned 401 `unauthorized`, and ts …003 is in neither database file. The records of the two accepted fixes (ts …000, …001) are still in the WAL. Caveat: a WAL keeps old page frames, so this does not strictly prove that no later frame removed them.

findings.body: Extra checks, all as the specifications say. Panel POST /telemetry/verify-r3-phone with the fingerprint header returned 404 with an empty body (FR-TELEMETRY-008). Device-API POST without the header returned 401 with the same `unauthorized` body. POST /devices on 8080 returned 404, so there is no network enrolment. None of the rejected requests (ts …002 to …005) left a fix, and none moved last_contact past the second accepted fix. CLI: set-fingerprint on an unknown id exited 1 (`no device no-such-device`); `add` with `dd:dd` exited 2 (`invalid fingerprint: 64 hexadecimal characters, no separators`); `add` with an existing id exited 1 (`device verify-r3-phone already exists`).

Verification limit, not a product defect. Nothing on the surface shows stored fixes or last contact, and this stage may run only curl and cargo run, so I checked stored state with byte-pattern searches over the SQLite files. ripgrep does not search binary files in directory mode, so every search named a file and had a positive control. They show last_contact == received_at to the millisecond for the first fix. They cannot strictly prove that earlier fixes were never deleted after revocation. An `ATALAYA_DATABASE_PATH=… cargo run` prefix is refused, so I used `cargo run --config 'env.ATALAYA_DATABASE_PATH="…"'`.
